articles.title: A skeptic spent the night hunting for Civil War ghosts. ‘Did you hear that?’
articles.summary: A skeptic hunts for ghosts at McRaven House, an antebellum home in Vicksburg, Mississippi, rife with bewitching tales from America’s winding past — and perhaps some residents who refuse to leave.
articles.body: Vicksburg, Mississippi (CNN) – Near closing time on a recent Fourth of July, Grace Bailey noticed a man approaching along the brick pathway, headed toward the front door of McRaven House in Vicksburg, Mississippi. Through the foliage lining the walk, she could see he was dressed more formally than the usual tourists at the antebellum home, whose first quarters were built in 1797. As one of two tour guides on duty, Bailey marched back inside to her post at the front door to greet the late-arriving guest. But when she opened the door, nobody was coming up the walk. While she stood waiting for the man to reappear, though, she realized something eerily familiar about his attire and distinctive hair style, both of which seemed out of place and time. Then, she remembered the other significance of the date: In Vicksburg, July 4th is also remembered as the day in 1863 when Confederate forces surrendered to the Union army, ending a grisly 43-day siege. And it was exactly one year after the siege ended that then-owner John H. Bobb was murdered by Union occupiers. “I was on the verge of freaking out, because the hair that I saw had the same swoosh as Mr. Bobb’s portrait,” Bailey says. “It was a moment of, ‘Okay, well, I just saw a ghost for officially the first time.’” Starvation, dismemberment and death are all part of the gruesome Civil War history in the Mississippi River city that President Lincoln called “the key” to defeating the Confederacy, and McRaven claims its own role in the narrative. During the campaign, this was one of the private residences used as a makeshift hospital for wounded Confederates, hundreds of whom are believed to be buried in a mass grave a scant 50 feet from the house. But as guides and guests alike insist, paranormal activity is a year-round occurrence at McRaven, and not solely tied to the war — so much that it hosts monthly late-night ghost hunts in addition to its historical tours. On an evening in September, I joined 13 other guests, including some repeat visitors, to attempt to connect with its spirits. Something goes bump Before we go any further, I must admit: I’m a skeptic about the supernatural. I’ve never seen, felt or heard a ghost, and I’ve never witnessed an inanimate object move of its own accord. To me, ghost stories seem too fantastical and detached from the reality I know. But I’ve also hedged against those beliefs; once, when I had to overnight in another alleged haunted house, I self-medicated enough to ensure nothing except the blast of my 7 a.m. alarm could rouse me. Bailey says she held a similar opinion when she started working at McRaven. “I was a skeptical believer. I was like, ‘maybe there’s ghosts.’ I wasn’t going to say anyone is weird for believing in ghosts, but I wasn’t quite convinced yet.” The fleeting glimpse she believes she caught of McRaven’s murdered owner convinced her. If McRaven House made a quick convert of Bailey, it wasted no time in its attempt to convince me, too. Not long after she and her colleague, Brian Riley, explained the ins and outs of the electronic gizmos that would supposedly help us locate spirits, a series of muted but definite thumps sounded from the unoccupied second floor. “Did you hear that?” I asked Jon Williams, a guest whom I had just met. “Yeah. That sounded like footsteps.” We shared a look of bemusement. It was barely 9 p.m., but the hunt was officially on. Williams, who traveled four hours from Booneville, Mississippi, was visiting for the second time with his wife, Cassie. Although he said he grew up in a house where he experienced ongoing paranormal activity, he didn’t expect much the first time he and his wife toured McRaven. “I was thinking it was just a tourist trap-type thing,” he says. “I mean, you walk up on an old house like that, set in the woods, it’s gonna feel creepy whether there’s anything there or not.” He soon changed his mind. In the upstairs bedroom of Mary Elizabeth Howard, a teenage bride who died during childbirth in 1836, he said he witnessed an armoire repeatedly open and close on its own. Across a hallway in the original section of the home, where Civil War relics like a bone saw and a blood-stained cloth stretcher are displayed, his wife, Cassie, said she had an encounter in the bedroom of Andrew Glass, the notorious highwayman and thief who built the first phase of McRaven. As she stood in the small quarters, where an antique four-poster bed draped with sheer white curtains casts a cadaverous pall, she said she felt something touching her hair. She assumed it was her three-year-old son, whom she was holding, until she saw his hands were nowhere near her head. Staffers say the ghost of Glass gravitates toward women, and Bailey, the guide, believes he is responsible for her own first paranormal experience at McRaven. She said that incident, which wasn’t an actual sighting, consisted of a gentle grabbing of her ankle and something brushing against her cheek. A few minutes past 11 p.m., the Williamses and I stood in the Glass bedroom with Bailey and a few other guests when something began to register on a K2 EMF meter and REM-pod, two gadgets purported to measure changes in temperature and electromagnetic fields consistent with paranormal visits. Bailey, with headphones on, listened as the spirit box raced through radio frequencies for answers to questions the guests asked. Among the “responses” was a string of obscenities. The scene was tense as we watched for more signs of life. Then, the activity abruptly stopped. “For sure, there was something there,” Bailey says. Across the hall, Mary Elizabeth’s room was quiet, with only a few discernible words coming across the spirit box. It’s typically one of the most active rooms, and during one memorable hunt, Riley says he observed a baton owned by her husband, who served as sheriff, move on its own. Riley, a veteran of paranormal research who led a separate group that night, says he has witnessed shadowy figures darting through the azaleas around the same time of year Bailey saw the man come up the walk. By his account, he’s been knocked down and scratched, and once during a tour, he says he locked eyes with a strange woman on the second-floor balcony outside Mary Elizabeth’s bedroom — a particularly chilling moment, since she wasn’t on the tour and was never seen again. “I think she noticed me, and I definitely noticed her,” Riley says. “I remember she had brown eyes, brown hair pulled back in a bun, and a brown dress with blue flowers. I was later told that particular style was an 1830s dress.” In his telling, activity increased, he says, after one of the owners accidentally unearthed a human femur while digging a shallow trench to bury electrical wires. Riley had just arrived at the house to prepare for a tour when he says he saw a shadowy figure step off the front porch and walk toward the back of the house. Again, the figure was never seen again. “I think there could be a correlation with that,” he says, “because I remember for a couple of days, the house kind of seemed unsettled.” A party of spirits? Around 12:45 a.m., we moved downstairs to the parlor, a gathering space adorned with ornate fixtures, a baby grand piano, and elaborate crown molding original to the 1849 addition. With headphones on, Bailey listened to the spirit box and repeated the words “party” and “mask” as she deciphered them through the static. A REM-pod placed in the center of the room began flashing while a small LED cat toy placed on the mantle flickered to life after Cassie Williams asked if the spirits were having a party. Another guest asked if it was a masquerade ball; again, the gadgets responded, whether by coincidence or something else. Later in the same area, a spirit box app on her husband Jon’s phone flashed the name “Ida” — coincidentally (or not), the name of a woman who died in the house in 1946. “I’ve never seen Mary’s room that quiet on a ghost hunt before, especially that early in the night,” Bailey says, “but the parlor made up for that in a way, because there was very much an increase of activity that specific night. They were probably having a party and we interrupted them.” “When we were in Miss Mary Elizabeth’s room,” Cassie Williams says, the spirit box “kept saying that she was saying, ‘Late,’ and, ‘Get out.’ And I was like, I wonder if she was late to the party because we were disturbing her, and she told us to get out so she could go.” At nearly 1:30 in the morning, that all seemed plausible. Were we interlopers bumming out their good time? As my exhaustion broke the spell of curiosity, the narrative appealed to me. It was time to leave these ghosts to their revelry, if that’s what it was, and retire from the hunt. In groups of two and three, the other guests began to drop out and head to their cars, and I soon followed — careful, I must admit, to make sure nothing followed me on the way out. As I walked along the brick pathway, reversing the mysterious walk that made a believer out of Bailey, I tried to shake the thought I was being watched. I emerged into the hazy light beaming down from a pair of utility poles, crossed the pavement of Harrison Street, which dead-ends at McRaven, and made a brisk retreat to my vehicle, now sitting by itself at the far end of the gravel parking lot. Then, in one fluid motion, I locked the doors, cranked the engine, and threw the transmission into drive.

articles.title: Reconstrução de ponte sobre o Rio Tocantins deve custar R$ 430 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Ponte atual entre Pedro Afonso e Tupirama, na região central do estado, será demolida após estudo apontar falhas graves. Caminhões e outros veículos pesados precisam atravessar o rio de balsa.
articles.summary: Ponte atual entre Pedro Afonso e Tupirama, na região central do estado, será demolida após estudo apontar falhas graves. Caminhões e outros veículos pesados precisam atravessar o r
articles.body:
O Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes (Dnit) publicou nesta sexta-feira (23) o edital de licitação para a construção de uma nova ponte sobre o Rio Tocantins, na BR-235, entre Pedro Afonso e Tupirama, na região central do estado. A obra está estimada em R$ 430 milhões.

A ponte atual foi condenada pelo Dnit após um estudo apontar falhas graves na estrutura, em agosto de 2026 . O tráfego chegou a ser totalmente interditado, mas a passagem de carros de passeio e motocicletas foi liberada posteriormente.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Caminhões e outros veículos pesados precisam atravessar o rio de balsa. Durante a estiagem, as embarcações chegaram a encalhar no Rio Tocantins, deixando motoristas ilhados por mais de 18 horas.

O aviso de licitação foi publicado no Diário Oficial da União nesta sexta-feira (23). Segundo o edital, a empresa contratada será responsável pelos estudos, pela elaboração dos projetos básico e executivo de engenharia, pela execução das obras, incluindo a demolição e a reconstrução, além do monitoramento contínuo da ponte sobre o Rio Tocantins, na BR-235.

A licitação adotará o critério de menor preço. A abertura das propostas está prevista para 22 de janeiro de 2027. Ainda não há data definida para o início das obras.

Ponte sobre o Rio Tocantins, na BR-235 liga Pedro Afonso a Tupirama — Foto: Foto: Luciano Ribeiro/Governo do Tocantins

A interdição da ponte no km 163 da BR-235 começou em 21 de maio de 2026, após vistorias identificarem problemas estruturais. Inicialmente, apenas veículos com carga acima de quatro toneladas estavam proibidos de passar, mas a restrição evoluiu para o fechamento total por medida preventiva.

A região é um importante corredor de escoamento da produção agroindustrial do Matopiba. Em razão dos prejuízos logísticos e econômicos gerados pelo bloqueio, a Prefeitura de Pedro Afonso decretou situação de emergência por 180 dias.

Para minimizar os transtornos, o Governo do Tocantins autorizou a operação emergencial de balsas para realizar a travessia entre Pedro Afonso e Tupirama, serviço que começou a operar de forma temporária enquanto o Dnit aprofundava os estudos técnicos agora concluídos.

Batizada de Ponte Prefeito Leôncio Miranda, a travessia possui 1.060 metros de extensão, 24 pilares e foi inaugurada em dezembro de 2007. A obra custou R$ 92,7 milhões em uma parceria entre a União e o Governo do Tocantins para facilitar o escoamento da produção agrícola da região.

articles.title: Ex-FBIs são acusados de mentir em caso envolvendo filho de Biden | G1
articles.standfirst: Nikki Floris e Bradley Benavides são acusados de dar declarações falsas ao Congresso sobre sua atuação em investigações relacionadas ao laptop de Hunter Biden.
articles.summary: Nikki Floris e Bradley Benavides são acusados de dar declarações falsas ao Congresso sobre sua atuação em investigações relacionadas ao laptop de Hunter Biden.
articles.body:
Hunter Biden, filho de Joe Biden, em 3 de junho de 2024 — Foto: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

Dois ex-funcionários do FBI foram acusados de mentir ao Congresso sobre seu envolvimento nas investigações relacionadas ao laptop de Hunter Biden , filho do ex-presidente americano Joe Biden , antes das eleições presidenciais de 2020.

O caso é o mais recente de uma série de medidas de grande repercussão e forte teor político adotadas pelo Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos antes das eleições de meio de mandato de novembro.

Nikki Floris e Bradley Benavides foram dirigentes de uma força-tarefa do FBI criada para combater a interferência estrangeira nas eleições e posteriormente extinta.

Na sexta-feira, os dois compareceram a um tribunal federal em Washington, onde seus advogados pediram uma audiência rápida para contestar as acusações de que eles mentiram a parlamentares sobre seu envolvimento nas investigações do FBI sobre Hunter Biden.

O processo, um raro caso criminal do Departamento de Justiça contra ex-funcionários da pasta, retoma uma controvérsia que agitou as últimas semanas da campanha eleitoral de 2020.

O caso também ocorre em meio a uma iniciativa mais ampla do diretor do FBI, Kash Patel, para reexaminar episódios de grande repercussão do passado recente da agência que, por anos, mobilizaram a base conservadora do presidente Donald Trump . Antes de assumir o comando do FBI, Patel era um crítico ferrenho da instituição.

Os advogados de Floris a chamaram de “patriota” e afirmaram que ela “serviu nossa nação como uma dedicada agente de inteligência do FBI por quase 20 anos”.

“Hoje, no entanto, o Departamento de Justiça a acusou falsamente de um crime com base na palavra de políticos, não nos fatos”, disseram seus advogados em comunicado. “Não é coincidência que o governo esteja apresentando essas acusações absurdas agora, anos depois, às vésperas de uma eleição.”

Os advogados de Benavides acusaram o governo de apresentar “acusações criminais infundadas contra ele em um processo claramente político”.

“Este é mais um dia triste para o Departamento de Justiça”, disseram seus advogados em comunicado enviado por e-mail. “Mas agora estamos no tribunal, e a verdade virá à tona: Brad Benavides é um verdadeiro patriota que dedicou sua carreira a proteger este país e seu povo. Essas acusações são uma vergonha.”

Acusação ocorre a poucos dias das eleições de meio de mandato

O processo foi aberto dez dias antes das eleições de 3 de novembro, por meio de um "criminal complaint", instrumento que permite apresentar formalmente acusações antes de o caso ser submetido a um grande júri, responsável por decidir se há base suficiente para um indiciamento. O Departamento de Justiça tem enfrentado dificuldades em casos de grande repercussão para obter acusações formais de grandes júris em Washington.

Durante a audiência, tanto os advogados de defesa quanto o juiz chamaram atenção para a forma incomum como a acusação foi apresentada. Esse tipo de procedimento costuma ser utilizado pelos promotores quando há necessidade urgente de deter um investigado, por exemplo, por risco de fuga ou por representar perigo à comunidade.

O juiz federal Zia Faruqui afirmou ser incomum que acusações relacionadas a fatos ocorridos anos atrás sejam apresentadas dessa maneira. Apesar do pedido dos promotores por mais tempo, ele marcou uma audiência preliminar para terça-feira (27) e afirmou que o processo representava uma “espada de Dâmocles” sobre os réus.

Laptop de Hunter Biden virou tema da eleição de 2020

A revelação da existência do laptop, em outubro de 2020, adicionou um novo elemento à disputa entre Donald Trump, então presidente e candidato republicano à reeleição, e Joe Biden, pai de Hunter e candidato democrata que acabou vencendo a eleição.

O caso ganhou repercussão após o New York Post publicar informações extraídas do laptop. O jornal afirmou ter recebido de Rudy Giuliani, aliado de Trump, o disco rígido de um computador que Hunter Biden teria deixado em uma assistência técnica em Wilmington, no estado de Delaware, cerca de um ano antes.

O caso retoma antigas críticas de republicanos no Congresso à forma como o FBI lidou com o laptop. Entre elas está a alegação de que a agência não deixou claro ao público que o material contido no computador, incluindo e-mails sobre negócios de Hunter Biden no exterior, era autêntico e não resultado de desinformação russa.

As circunstâncias da descoberta do laptop levantaram suspeitas entre democratas e ex-integrantes dos serviços de inteligência sobre um possível envolvimento russo.

Na época, a comunidade de inteligência do governo Trump havia avaliado que Moscou tentava interferir nas eleições em favor do republicano, enquanto Giuliani buscava no exterior informações que pudessem comprometer a família Biden. Dezenas de ex-funcionários da inteligência americana assinaram uma carta afirmando que o caso apresentava as “características clássicas de uma operação de informação russa”.

Mas o então diretor de Inteligência Nacional, John Ratcliffe, afirmou em carta ao Congresso que não havia provas de envolvimento de agentes estrangeiros com o laptop. Posteriormente, o FBI, então comandado por Christopher Wray, corroborou essa avaliação.

Hunter Biden foi condenado em processos relacionados à posse ilegal de arma e a crimes fiscais durante o governo de seu pai. Joe Biden concedeu perdão presidencial ao filho nas últimas semanas de seu mandato.

Caso envolve força-tarefa criada para combater influência estrangeira

Segundo a acusação, Floris e Benavides, que ocupavam cargos de liderança na Força-Tarefa de Influência Estrangeira (FITF, na sigla em inglês), estavam diretamente envolvidos nas investigações sobre Hunter Biden, que era tema recorrente nas reuniões do grupo.

Segundo a acusação, porém, os dois minimizaram o que sabiam diretamente sobre o laptop e o grau de envolvimento nas investigações durante depoimentos prestados em 2023 a parlamentares que também investigavam Hunter Biden.

A acusação sustenta que Benavides mentiu ao dizer que soube pela Wikipédia que o FBI estava de posse do laptop. Segundo o documento, Floris também teria mentido ao afirmar que não sabia que Hunter Biden havia sido tema de discussões na FITF.

“Quando altos funcionários do FBI mentem ao Congresso, isso atinge o cerne do nosso sistema. Ninguém está acima da lei”, afirmou Patel.

O caso volta a colocar em evidência o trabalho da força-tarefa, criada durante o primeiro mandato de Trump para combater campanhas de influência da Rússia e de outros países destinadas a semear discórdia, enfraquecer a democracia e disseminar desinformação.

O grupo tornou-se alvo de críticas de republicanos no Congresso, em parte por sua atuação em questões relacionadas a Hunter Biden, e foi dissolvido em fevereiro de 2025 pela então procuradora-geral Pam Bondi.

Governo Trump ampliou ações envolvendo adversários políticos

Como diretor do FBI, Patel supervisionou demissões em massa de agentes envolvidos em investigações sobre Trump ou vistos como contrários à agenda do governo republicano.

Ele também voltou sua atenção para investigações anteriores à sua gestão, como as relacionadas a Hunter Biden, que foram alvo de críticas de aliados de Trump.

Historicamente, o Departamento de Justiça procura evitar, no período próximo às eleições, medidas públicas em investigações envolvendo candidatos ou que possam influenciar o resultado político.

Nas últimas duas semanas, porém, autoridades adotaram uma série de ações de forte repercussão política. Entre elas estão uma busca na casa da deputada democrata Ilhan Omar, no âmbito de uma investigação sobre fraude imigratória, e uma acusação de corrupção anunciada na quinta-feira (22) contra L. Louise Lucas, influente senadora estadual democrata da Virgínia.

Omar e Lucas são críticas de Trump. Omar, deputada por Minnesota, classificou a busca em sua casa em Washington como uma “tentativa de atingir inimigos políticos e usar as forças de segurança federais como arma”. Lucas afirmou que não se deixará intimidar ou pressionar pelo governo federal e que “não recuará”.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Marroquina faz sinal internacional de socorro e é salva pela PM | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher pediu ajuda ao ver policiais, que algemaram e detiveram marido marroquino por violência doméstica. Denúncia foi feita pela enteada da vítima na sexta (23). Família é de refugiados.
articles.summary: Mulher pediu ajuda ao ver policiais, que algemaram e detiveram marido marroquino por violência doméstica. Denúncia foi feita pela enteada da vítima. Família é de refugiados.
articles.body:
Uma mulher marroquina, integrante de uma família de refugiados acolhida no Brasil, foi resgatada com um bebê no colo pela Polícia Militar (PM) após fazer o sinal silencioso internacional de socorro de dentro da casa onde mora, na Vila Maria, Zona Norte de São Paulo. O caso aconteceu na sexta-feira (23) e foi registrado pela câmera corporal de um dos policiais que atenderam a ocorrência (veja vídeo acima) .

Segundo a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP), a denúncia foi feita pela filha do homem acusado de violência doméstica contra a esposa. A adolescente, de 13 anos, acionou o telefone 190. Paralelamente, uma funcionária da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) que atua no apoio a refugiados também procurou as autoridades após receber um pedido de ajuda da vítima.

Quando os policiais chegaram ao endereço, e entraram na casa, a mulher fez o sinal internacional de socorro, um gesto reconhecido mundialmente para pedidos silenciosos de ajuda em situações de violência. O movimento consiste em mostrar a palma da mão, dobrar o polegar para dentro e fechar os demais dedos sobre ele.

Câmera corporal da PM mostra marroquina fazer sinal silencioso internacional de socorro. Em seguida, marido é detido por suspeita de violência doméstica. — Foto: Reprodução/PM-SP

As imagens da câmera corporal mostram o momento em que um dos agentes percebe o pedido de ajuda da mulher, que segurava uma criança.

"Eu não entender o português", afirma a marroquina, que faz o gesto. "Ela fez sinal", responde o policial ao alertar os colegas.

Diante da confirmação de que a mulher pedia socorro, os agentes retiraram a mulher e o bebê da residência. Segundo a SSP, o homem estava alterado e foi afastado da vítima para garantir a segurança dela. O vídeo ainda mostra o marido sendo algemado e detido durante a ocorrência.

Com a situação controlada, os policiais passaram a conversar com a mulher com auxílio de um aplicativo de tradução de idioma no celular. Como ela não fala português, a ferramenta convertia para o árabe as mensagens ditas pelos agentes e traduzia para o português as respostas da vítima.

Refugiada marroquina conversa com PM com ajuda do tradutor de idioma no celular. — Foto: Reprodução/PM-SP

Em determinado momento, um dos PMs tenta tranquilizá-la e fala ao celular para que a mensagem seja traduzida: "Pode ficar tranquila. Hoje você não vai voltar. Fica tranquila", diz o policial.

A ferramenta permitiu que a vítima relatasse o que havia acontecido dentro da residência. A equipe permaneceu no local prestando assistência à mulher e aos familiares. A funcionária da ONU também acompanhou o atendimento e auxiliou na comunicação.

A ocorrência foi encaminhada para a 4ª Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM), responsável pela investigação do caso.

A reportagem procurou a SSP para saber se o homem continuava detido após o registro da ocorrência e se ele foi indiciado por violência doméstica. Até a última atualização deste texto, não havia retorno.

O que é o sinal internacional de socorro

O gesto utilizado pela marroquina é reconhecido internacionalmente como um pedido silencioso de ajuda em situações de violência. Criado para permitir que vítimas alertem terceiros sem chamar a atenção do agressor, ele consiste em mostrar a palma da mão, dobrar o polegar para dentro e fechar os demais dedos sobre ele.

No caso da Vila Maria, o reconhecimento imediato do sinal pelos policiais foi determinante para que a vítima conseguisse pedir ajuda mesmo sem conseguir se comunicar em português.

articles.title: Protestos na França: polícia usa gás lacrimogêneo em Lyon e Pau; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Lyon, a terceira maior cidade da França, os agentes dispararam as bombas de efeito moral depois que os manifestantes tentaram bloquear rua. Houve um pequeno confronto.
articles.summary: Em Lyon, a terceira maior cidade da França, os agentes dispararam as bombas de efeito moral depois que os manifestantes tentaram bloquear rua. Houve um pequeno confronto.
articles.body:
A polícia usou gás lacrimogêneo para conter o início de tumultos durante protestos nas cidades de Lyon e Pau, no sul da França, neste sábado (24).

Em Lyon, a terceira maior cidade da França, os agentes dispararam as bombas de efeito moral depois que os manifestantes, que protestavam perto de uma faculdade universitária e da delegacia de polícia da cidade, tentaram bloquear uma rua. Houve um pequeno confronto com alguns deles.

Em Pau, uma testemunha registrou em vídeo o momento em que uma correria começou depois que o gás foi lançado.

De acordo com a agência de notícias AFP, os policiais também usaram granadas de gás lacrimogêneo em Lille, Toulouse e Nantes.

Policiais dispersam multidão com bombas de gás lacrimogêneo em Lyon — Foto: REUTERS/Lisi Niesner

Apesar dos incidentes, até o começo da tarde deste sábado, não haviam sido registrados grandes incidentes nos atos autorizados pelo governo para ocorrerem.

Em Paris , a manifestação começou de forma pacífica, com centenas de pessoas reunidas nas ruas da capital francesa.

Centenas de pessoas reunidas em manifestação em Paris neste sábado (24) — Foto: REUTERS/Abdul Saboor

Segundo o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nunez, 135 pessoas fora presas em todo o país , mas muitas das prisões ocorreram após buscas preventivas que também resultaram na apreensão de itens que poderiam ser usados ​​como armas . Entre eles, bolas de metal, chumbinhos, fogos de artifício, estilingues, balas de aço, armas improvisadas, uma katana e armas de airsoft.

"Temos que ser extremamente ágeis. Recebemos muitos pedidos de interrupção por parte de grupos políticos e, simplesmente, de criminosos. Vai ser um dia longo", afirmou ele a repórteres.

Os principais museus de Paris fecharam neste sábado (24) devido à previsão de novas manifestações.

O Louvre, o Museu d'Orsay, o Museu Picasso e o Grand Palais — onde está em cartaz uma importante exposição de Cézanne —, entre outros, decidiram fechar aos turistas. A Art Basel, uma das feiras de arte contemporânea mais prestigiadas do mundo, cancelou parte de sua programação e abriu ao público apenas nesta sexta-feira (23).

Aviso de fechamento na porta do Louvre — Foto: REUTERS/Dylan Martinez

Há uma semana, cerca de 3.000 lojas em toda a França foram danificadas ou saqueadas. Nos últimos dias, com a convocação para novas manifestações neste sábado, comerciantes barricaram suas lojas.

As manifestações contra o alto custo de vida já reuniram mais de 500 mil pessoas , segundo estimativas da imprensa do país. Elas foram acompanhadas por repressão policial e c erca de 1.800 pessoas foram presas no sábado passado (17) .

Barricada sendo montada na porta de loja — Foto: REUTERS/Pedro Nunes

Manifestações têm restrições em grandes cidades

As autoridades autorizaram atos em pelo menos oito grandes cidades neste sábado, segundo um levantamento da agência de notícias AFP. As regras, porém, variam de município para município .

Em Paris , a polícia aprovou um percurso entre as praças da Bastilha e da Nação, organizado por sindicatos. No entanto, a manifestação de coletivos estudantis e de integrantes dos coletes amarelos, entre a Bastilha e a Ópera de Paris , foi proibida.

Em Marselha, a segunda maior do país, um protesto sindical foi autorizado excepcionalmente, depois que as autoridades locais haviam proibido manifestações na cidade.

articles.body: Two senior military observers have reported seeing a mysterious black triangular object travelling at an estimated 1,800mph over a sensitive site in the western United States earlier this year, according to a report released by the Trump administration on Friday.The observers described the unidentified object as unlike any conventional military aircraft. According to their account submitted to the defence department, it disappeared suddenly and silently within seconds, without leaving an exhaust trail or any other visible evidence, the Guardian reported.The object was said to resemble a delta-wing drone, with an estimated wingspan of between nine and 15 feet (2.75 to 4.5 metres). The report classified it as an “unidentified anomalous phenomenon” (UAP), the term increasingly used by military and government agencies instead of UFO.The location of the alleged sighting has been redacted in the report. The observers were described as having “extensive operational experience working alongside government agencies”.However, the document offers limited visual evidence to support the account. It contains nine identical images of a canyon, with small triangular silhouettes superimposed on the landscape to illustrate the object's reported movement.Pentagon's UFO disclosuresThe latest release is part of a series of documents made public by the Pentagon since May, following US President Donald Trump's pledge to disclose previously classified information about UFO sightings and the government's knowledge of potential extraterrestrial life.Trump ordered a broader disclosure in February, following years of public scrutiny and allegations of a government cover-up.In 2023, a former intelligence official told Congress that successive administrations had concealed information about UFOs and that the government possessed crashed alien spacecraft. Those allegations have not established that extraterrestrial craft exist.The pace of disclosures has slowed in recent months, with Friday's release containing fewer than 25 text documents and no videos or photographs. While several earlier reports included photographs or footage of alleged sightings, the black-triangle account relies on observers' descriptions and illustrative images.The report does not establish the object's identity or provide independent evidence confirming the observers' account.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2010, while tracing Trosley’s history with Google Earth, Kent volunteers followed crop marks to a Roman villa; excavation revealed a bathhouse, painted walls and underfloor heating
articles.summary: A community excavation led by Kent Archaeological Society volunteers uncovered a high-status Roman villa near Trosley, revealing a rare bathhouse, painted walls, and advanced heating systems, thanks to innovative crop mark detection through Google Earth.
articles.body: The Kent Archaeological Society runs the ongoing Trosley Heritage Project, which Current Archaeology describes as a larger landscape project studying how Trosley has been inhabited over time. Part of this work is done at the desk, with members searching publicly available satellite imagery of the fields for signs of buried features. Because crops can grow differently above buried walls and ditches, creating crop marks visible in satellite imagery even when they are not apparent at ground level, volunteers noticed a distinctive pattern in farmland near the village. Kent’s Historic Environment Record provides the relevant heritage record. The Society later held a community excavation of the site, with residents working alongside the Society’s more experienced excavators and the dig also hosted school visits. The dig uncovered partial foundations of what may have been a high-status Roman villa, along with painted wall plaster and remains of the villa’s hypocaust system.Crop marks in Google Earth images from 2007 and earlier finds of Roman building materialThe Kent Historic Environment Record entry titled Possible Romano-British building, Trottiscliffe describes a faint cropmark visible in Google Earth images from 2007 and in aerial photographs from 2008. It is described on record as two squares connected by a rectangle, around 28 metres in length but no wider than 14 metres. The same record notes that roof tiles, box flue tiles, fragments of painted plaster and coins dating from the 3rd and 4th centuries were found in a field north of Trottiscliffe and that fieldwalking there turned up Roman roofing tile and pottery together with mortared rubble suggesting a buried Roman masonry structure, perhaps a villa.The Society’s own report, Roman villa with bathhouse and hypocaust system revealed near Trosley, written by Jacob Scott, appeared in issue 119 (Winter 2022) of the Kent Archaeological Society magazine. It describes how crop markings were spotted on Google Earth after a particularly dry period, which led to fieldwalking and test pits in the year before the excavation. The cropmark projections created by Chris Blair-Myers were used for trench placement. Current Archaeology, as reported by The Past, says the Society first found the site in 2010 during a survey of Google Earth images, while the 2007 date given by the record and the Society refers to the date of the images that showed the cropmarks.The September 2022 community excavation and what trench 1 revealedIn excess of 50 volunteers assisted with the September 2022 excavation directed by site director Richard Taylor, according to The Past in its write-up of issue 394 of Current Archaeology. Trench 1, which was dug on the main building, revealed foundations of the villa made of local ragstone and flint. Third and fourth-century ceramics found at the site include local coarse wares, Oxfordshire wares and some Samian wares alongside several coins dating back to the 4th century.The Kent Archaeological Society magazine report also mentions a quantity of multicoloured painted wall plaster from Trench 1, which likely adorned the villa’s interior walls. Archaeology magazine lists a fourth-century copper-alloy strap-end shaped like an amphora, a small Romano-British key and two fourth-century coins. For many volunteers, it was a first excavation, Taylor told Artnet News and he pointed out that most archaeology in Kent is developer-led, which makes openings for volunteers uncommon. The same report says the Society first identified the villa complex from Google Earth images and that volunteers later helped excavate trenches over the main building and what is believed to be a bathhouse.A pilae stack at least 11 tiles high and a rare surviving hypocaustOther trenches discovered the foundations of a bathhouse and a pilae stack, which is an upright stack of tiles that supported the floor above the heating room. The Past describes how it had risen to at least 11 tiles, but the bottom tile remains to be excavated. At some time, possibly during the 4th century, the bath house seems to have been filled up and converted into another structure. The metalled surface of compacted flints was discovered west of the bath house structure. Taylor said in a statement, reported by Artnet News, that among the hundreds of villas across Kent, a surviving hypocaust is rare. Archaeology magazine includes his assertion that running the hypocaust was costly because it needed an uninterrupted supply of wood fuel and a labor force to run it.Farming wealth and the September 2023 return to Trosley CourtTaylor told Artnet News that the occupants probably farmed the surrounding land and sold their crops in London, Canterbury or Gaul. The Society’s magazine report said it planned to return in September 2023 to investigate the bathhouse further and the Society’s own later page on the site states that its 2023 excavations at Trosley Court revealed a Romano-British bathhouse.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Largest ever’: Elon Musk donates $443 million to Trump's campaign ahead of US midterms
articles.summary: Billionaire Elon Musk has spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, emerging
articles.body: Billionaire Elon Musk has spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, emerging as the largest individual political donor in US history.Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings show that Musk made three direct contributions totalling $74.8 million to his America PAC between October 6 and 14, Forbes reported. An additional $1.98 million came through his company, United States of America Inc., taking his total contributions for the first half of October to nearly $77 million.America PAC is a political action committee founded and heavily backed by Musk to support Republican and conservative candidates through voter turnout operations and digital campaigns.According to Forbes, America PAC reported spending approximately $42.7 million during the first two weeks of October, with $46.5 million in cash remaining as of October 14.The PAC has reported around $68.6 million in independent expenditures during the current midterm election cycle, primarily targeting competitive Senate races, according to FEC records compiled by the PaidForPolitics tracker.Texas senate race gets largest share of spendingThe largest share of the PAC's spending has gone towards the Texas Senate race. It has spent $27.9 million opposing Democratic candidate James Talarico and another $4.8 million supporting his Republican opponent, Ken Paxton. Forbes reported.America PAC has also spent approximately $9.3 million on the Ohio Senate race, followed by $7.7 million in Michigan, $2.7 million in Iowa and $2.1 million in Maine. The spending in these states has primarily focused on opposing Democratic candidates.Earlier this month, The New York Times reported that Musk had contributed more than $366 million to midterm election races by the end of September, including donations to America PAC and other outside groups.That figure included a $158 million donation to the Republican Senate Leadership Fund last month. The super PAC subsequently transferred an identical amount to the Texas PAC, which supports Paxton's campaign.Forbes estimated Musk's net worth at $909.8 billion as of late Thursday night, retaining his position as the world's richest person.You use AI every day. articles.title: In a 2010 Italian field study, researchers mixed solar-dried orange peel into steep soil plots; after 20 rain events, soil erosion was about 50% lower under the tested conditions
articles.summary: A 2010 study in Italy demonstrates that solar-dried orange peel can significantly decrease soil erosion on steep land, with findings showing a 50% reduction in erosion rates, highlighting its potential as a sustainable agricultural practice.
articles.body: Soil erosion can gradually strip away the fertile surface layer that plants depend on, especially on steep land exposed to heavy rainfall. Protection of slope areas has remained an issue to be solved by farmers and landowners. Several studies have been done to check whether agricultural residues, normally wasted after processing the food materials, can provide a solution to this problem. A 2010 study by Bombino and colleagues in southern Italy checked whether solar-dried citrus peel could help control runoff and soil erosion. The study results indicated that orange peel, which is normally left after producing juice, was effective in reducing soil erosion.Eight experimental plots tested the citrus-peel treatmentAccording to Bombino and colleagues’ 2010 paper on land spreading of solar-dried citrus peel, the experiment used eight plots, each measuring 2 square metres, arranged in two wooden boxes set at a 100% slope. In four plots, the researchers added citrus peel, while the remaining four were left untreated. The 100% slope indicates that the vertical rise is the same as the horizontal distance. Solar-dried citrus peel was shredded into small pieces (4 to 8 mm) and mixed into the top 3 cm of soil at a rate of 3 kg per square metre. Then, the plots were subjected to natural rainfall and the researchers were able to observe runoff and sediment loss in treated and untreated soils under field conditions. The experiment was conducted during 20 rain events. Different rainfall conditions and plots with different ground cover properties were observed.Soil erosion fell by about 50%According to Bombino and colleagues, the key result was a 50% reduction in soil erosion in the treated plots compared with the controls. There was a 10% average decrease in the surface runoff as well. During this experiment, sediment yield and sediment concentration were, on average, 55-60% less in treated plots than in the controls. The decrease in runoff varied depending on observations and reached up to 33% at maximum. Runoff is the water flowing over the soil surface, whereas sediment yield is the soil carried out of the plot. In other words, despite the small decrease in runoff volumes, the decrease in soil loss may be much higher. The results suggest that solar-dried citrus peel can help minimize erosion under the tested conditions. Yet, it does not mean that the same effect will take place under other conditions.Organic matter may have improved soil conditionsThe study authors hypothesized that adding citrus peel would improve soil quality and promote plant growth. Organic material affects soil structure and the passage of water and could thus aid in the passage of rainwater into the soil instead of running on top of it. Plants are able to act as a shield from raindrops and slow down surface water. Plant roots might also play a role in keeping soil particles bound together. Improved soil quality and plant development were two possible explanations offered for decreased erosion. This interpretation needs to be carefully qualified. While there were clear distinctions made between treated and untreated plots in the experiment, there was no way of proving the degree to which each potential mechanism contributed to the decreased erosion.Citrus waste also requires careful handlingUsing citrus peel on land could provide a useful outlet for waste from fruit-processing industries. However, applying organic waste to soil also requires consideration of what happens as it decomposes and releases liquid. A later study, Evaluating the Pollution Risk of Soil Due to Natural Drainage of Orange Peel: First Results, published in Environments in 2021, investigated the potential pollution risk associated with drainage from orange peel. In their study, the scientists studied the organic liquid that came out of the substance under the conditions of the experiment. The authors concluded that the risk of soil pollution from natural drainage of orange peel was negligible, given the limited amounts of leachate and organic load, although they noted that heavy rainfall could aggravate the hazard.The paper reports three lysimeter tests on orange peel: one with raw peel left to drain naturally and two others exposed to 100 mm of simulated rainfall after the peel had already drained or been solar-dried. In about 14 weeks, the peel volume fell by roughly 90% and the raw-peel test released 37.7 L of leachate, about 19% of the initial peel volume. The authors found that the organic load reaching the soil was negligible. Unlike the erosion study conducted in 2010, this study raises a new question. In combination, the studies show the need to consider both the advantages and disadvantages of using agricultural waste.Further field testing is neededThe 2010 study by Bombino and colleagues suggests that solar-dried citrus peel can reduce soil erosion, but only under the specific experimental conditions tested. This information could be useful in any attempt to preserve lands which are either steep or erosion-prone, as well as discovering other uses for by-products from agriculture. Nevertheless, the experiment was carried out on a relatively small number of plots under certain conditions in southern Italy. Further research is needed to test the treatment in different soil types and climates and to assess how long the effect lasts. For now, the study only suggests that citrus peel may be useful in soil conservation, not that it is a guaranteed solution. The actual applicability of the material will depend on its efficiency in real-life situations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora on Saturday said she would not sign a bond to \"keep peace\" before a special executive
articles.body: NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora on Saturday said she would not sign a bond to "keep peace" before a special executive magistrate, a day after the Delhi high court dismissed her plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a Rs 10,000 bond with a surety."We don't have any conditions. We are not going to sign the bond," Bora said.Bora had moved the high court, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.She alleged that the proceedings were a "colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution".During Thursday's hearing, Bora's counsel argued that citizens did not need permission to hoist the national flag, referring to the police notice alleging that she had hoisted it without valid permission.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety "for keeping peace for a period of enquiry".Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.According to her petition, the police initiated proceedings over alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that she had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place that day."The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner's call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House," Bora's petition stated.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Iran on Saturday vowed not to allow US military ships into the Persian Gulf “under any circumstances”, as tensions with Washington escalated amid threats
articles.body: Iran on Saturday vowed not to allow US military ships into the Persian Gulf “under any circumstances”, as tensions with Washington escalated amid threats of further military action by the United States.Iran's armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi remarked after US President Donald Trump threatened another "little Epic Fury" to force Iran's compliance, in case negotiations fail.“We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,” Iranian state television quoted the chief of staff of Iran’s armed forces, Ali Abdollahi, as saying. AFP reported.“The US president must dream of seeing the armed forces enter the Persian Gulf. He will take that dream to his grave,” Abdollahi added.Iranian forces have restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key energy route connecting the Gulf to the wider world, since the war with the United States began on February 28. In response, Washington has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and vessels.Tehran has required ships to obtain permission to transit the strait and has repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to pass through a southern route near the Omani coast.According to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, several tankers attempting to use the route, which Tehran considers “illegal”, have been hit by mines in recent days.On Friday, the Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil had been abandoned at sea after striking mines in the strategic waterway. AFP reported.Possible strike on Iran this weekend?The latest warning from Tehran came after US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack said on Friday that a US strike on Iran could take place over the weekend, while stressing that Trump remained open to a diplomatic agreement.“Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely,” Barrack said in an interview with Lebanese-Australian entrepreneur Mario Nawfal on Friday.Barrack, who also serves as Trump’s special envoy, said the US president remained willing to negotiate but warned that continued threats against the United States, its allies and Gulf countries would have consequences.“The president has been clear. I'm giving you American policy. President is very clear. He's open and available and accessible to a deal. And we've been at the table for months and months and months,” Barrack said.Hours later, Trump addressed a rally in Florida where he told Americans that the possibility of further military action was open.“We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree,” Trump said.“If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business.' articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi made her debut on social media platform X on Saturday, sharing a video in which she
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi made her debut on social media platform X on Saturday, sharing a video in which she recalled her first meeting with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and offered a glimpse of her upcoming book, Belonging: A Journey of Love.The book, Sonia Gandhi's first, is scheduled to be launched on November 10. It recounts her personal journey, including her memories with Rajiv Gandhi and experiences from her younger days to the present.In the nearly two-minute video accompanying her first post on X, Sonia Gandhi recalled meeting Rajiv Gandhi at the Varsity Restaurant, a Greek eatery in Cambridge, England, where they were students.The video featured photographs of the couple and the restaurant where they first met."In a small Greek restaurant in Cambridge, my journey of love began. Rajiv and I created a world filled with love, laughter and memories. On 10th November, I share that world with you," she wrote in her post.Sonia Gandhi recalls meeting Rajiv Gandhi in CambridgeSpeaking in the video, the Congress MP recalled looking for Italian food while living in England, where she said the food available at the time did not suit her preferences."Food in England in those days was awful. In those days, you didn't have so many restaurants, you know, like you have today," she said.She explained that she was looking for a place serving food closer to what she was accustomed to, particularly Italian cuisine, when she discovered the Greek restaurant."And then, we discovered this place (Varsity Restaurant). It was a Greek restaurant where many European students, but also Indian students, used to go for their meals. And that is then where I met Rajiv in that very restaurant," she said.Recalling her first impression of Rajiv Gandhi, she said she felt almost immediately that he was someone she would want to spend her life with."When I first met him, I felt almost immediately that you know he was someone I would really love to be with. And, of course, I learned that it was the same for him," she said.Sonia Gandhi also recalled that a common friend introduced them. The two subsequently became friends and began attending parties with other students and visiting places together."I remember when I first met him, a friend, a common friend, introduced us. Then, you know, we became friends. Then going to parties with friends, or going to see sights, or… We went to a Valentine party where there were lots of students," she said.Describing what stood out to her about Rajiv Gandhi, she said his gentle nature had left a lasting impression."He was a very gentle-looking person. Of course, he was very good-looking. But that gentleness came through. So that was something which really touched me and struck me. So that, of course, I'll never forget when I first met him," she said.Sonia married Rajiv Gandhi on February 25, 1968.Upcoming memoir traces her personal journeyThe upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, explores Sonia Gandhi's life, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi to her move to India and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with her adopted country.Her debut on X comes two days after she joined Instagram on Thursday and shared a video offering a first look at the book.In her first Instagram post, she expressed gratitude at being able to share the preview with readers and described the memoir as a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong."I look forward to sharing it with you," she wrote in the post.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In the 1950s, a Kentucky family bought 37 acres and later added a smaller access parcel; decades after the two were sold separately, new owners lost their court fight to use the neighbour's driveway
articles.summary: A property dispute in Kentucky has ended with a state appeals court ruling against a couple who claimed they had the right to use a neighbour’s pathway to
articles.body: A property dispute in Kentucky has ended with a state appeals court ruling against a couple who claimed they had the right to use a neighbour’s pathway to reach their land. The dispute centred on two adjoining parcels that once belonged to the same family: a roughly 37-acre property bought in the 1950s and a smaller, three-fourths-acre tract acquired about 20 years later. For years, the family used a pathway across the smaller parcel to reach parts of the larger property. But after the two tracts were sold separately, the new owners disagreed over whether that access could continue.On October 23, 2026, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld a jury’s decision that Charlie E. Stearns and Kathy Stearns had no legal easement allowing them to cross the adjoining property owned by John Warinner and Betty Warinner. As reported by American legal website Law Justia, the court found that evidence supported the jury’s conclusion that the Stearnses did not have a legal right to use the route.Two adjoining properties, sold separatelyAccording to Law Justia, John Warinner’s parents bought the larger tract, approximately 37 acres, in the 1950s. About two decades later, they purchased the adjoining smaller tract, measuring three-fourths of an acre. The parents used a pathway on the smaller parcel to reach portions of the larger property. However, John Warinner testified that his parents had also used alternative routes for about 20 years before buying the smaller tract.After his parents died, the two parcels were sold separately by a court-appointed Master Commissioner on the same day. The Stearnses purchased the larger tract, which adjoined land they already owned. The Warinners bought the smaller parcel. The Stearnses believed they were entitled to continue using the pathway across the smaller property. The Warinners disagreed and eventually put up barriers to prevent access.The disagreement led to a lawsuit in 2022. The Warinners accused the Stearnses of wrongly claiming an easement across their land and also brought a trespass claim against them. The case went to a jury trial in February 2025.Why the couple said they needed the pathwayThe Stearnses argued that their right to use the route had developed while both parcels were under common ownership. Their claim relied on the idea that a property owner’s long-standing use of one part of a property to benefit another part can, in some circumstances, create an easement when ownership is later divided. They argued that the route was an implied easement, including an easement by necessity and what they described as an “apparent easement”.There was evidence supporting their position. Two of John Warinner’s sisters testified that the rough terrain made it extremely difficult, if not practically impossible, to reach the larger tract without crossing the smaller one. But other witnesses gave a different account. John Warinner said alternative access routes existed, and a surveyor testified that the Stearnses could reach the larger property without crossing the Warinners’ land.Warinner also identified an older road that could be used after repairs, although he acknowledged that it needed work before it would be usable. The appeals court said the evidence gave the jury a factual question to decide: whether crossing the smaller tract was reasonably necessary for access to the larger one.What the court said about an easement by necessityUnder Kentucky law, an easement by necessity generally requires common ownership before the properties were divided, a subsequent separation of ownership and a strict need to use the neighbouring property to obtain access. The appeals court said an easement by necessity generally cannot be established if the landowner has another way to reach a public road, even if that alternative is inconvenient.Because Warinner and the surveyor testified that other access was available, the court found there was enough evidence to support the jury’s rejection of the claim. The court also considered the argument that the pathway qualified as a ‘quasi-easement.’ This legal concept can arise when an owner uses one part of a property to benefit another and the use is sufficiently established, apparent and reasonably necessary to the land.The judges said the Stearnses had to show more than a history of using the pathway. They needed to establish that the route was reasonably necessary to the enjoyment of the larger tract. Evidence of alternative access meant the jury could reasonably find that this requirement had not been met.Kentucky does not recognise a separate “apparent easement” theoryThe Stearnses also argued that the pathway qualified as an apparent easement, a separate category they said could justify their access. According to Law Justia, the Court of Appeals rejected that argument. The judges also rejected the couple’s suggestion that the jury’s brief deliberations indicated that it had ignored evidence or committed misconduct. They said there was no concrete evidence of improper conduct. The jury had found that the Stearnses trespassed, but awarded the Warinners no damages on that claim.The appeals court concluded that the evidence supported the jury’s verdict and affirmed the lower court’s judgment. The opinion was marked “not to be published”. The ruling leaves the Stearnses without the claimed legal right to use the pathway across the Warinners’ smaller parcel. It also underlines a key point in property disputes: a route used for years does not automatically become a legally enforceable easement when neighbouring properties are sold separately.You use AI every day. articles.summary: MUMBAI: News coverage of the investigation into the firing at actor Tiger Shroff allegedly became a real-time alert system for the three shooters as they
articles.body: MUMBAI: News coverage of the investigation into the firing at actor Tiger Shroff allegedly became a real-time alert system for the three shooters as they fled Mumbai, with their handlers relaying updates through encrypted messaging applications and instructing them to change routes when their identities were exposed, police sources said on Saturday.The three accused were apprehended aboard a train in Kota on October 19, a day after the shooting in Mumbai’s Juhu area.Investigators believe that continuous updates about the police probe and the suspects’ movements prompted the trio to switch between modes of transport in an attempt to evade arrest.How handlers used news reports to guide the suspectsAccording to sources in the crime branch investigating the case, the handlers were monitoring television coverage and passing information directly to the shooters through encrypted Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) messaging applications.At one point during the escape, when news channels aired visuals of the attack, one of the main suspects allegedly received an urgent instruction on his mobile phone: “Tumhare chehre aa gaye hain, nikal jao waha se” (Your faces are out, get out of there).The actor escaped relatively unhurt on the evening of October 18 after two shooters fired multiple rounds at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area.The incident triggered a multi-state investigation, leading to the arrest of 10 people from Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana. Shroff’s driver and a vlogger sustained injuries in the firing.Signal, Zangi under scannerThe three key accused have been identified as Phool Singh (18), Rehan Rahisuddin Ansari (18) and Rithik Mahto (22). They were intercepted and arrested by Kota Police in Rajasthan on October 19 and are currently in police custody until October 31.Analysis of digital evidence indicated that Rehan was in constant contact with others through VoIP-based applications, crime branch sources said.Applications such as Signal and Zangi can be used for internet-based communication without requiring a mobile number for registration, they added.Police sources said reports about the recovery of the attackers’ motorcycle in Andheri and their subsequent train journey were also relayed to the shooters by their handlers.Shooters allegedly switched transport modesAccording to crime branch sources, the steady stream of updates prompted the trio to repeatedly change their mode of transport as they tried to escape.“This constant feed prompted the trio to frequently shift modes of transport, moving from a motorcycle to a train, followed by a cab, before planning to board a bus from Surat.“The delay at the Surat bus terminal eventually led them to board another train, where they were apprehended by the Kota police following a prompt alert from the Mumbai Police,” they said.The Crime Branch is questioning the accused in custody to establish how the firearms were procured and identify those involved in supplying weapons and providing logistical support.Mumbai Police have named gangster Anil Pandit as a wanted accused in the case. Pandit, an alleged associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang believed to be operating from the US, had claimed responsibility for the October 18 attack on Shroff in a social media post.The investigation is continuing, with police seeking to establish the roles of all those allegedly involved in planning and executing the firing, as well as those who provided weapons and logistical assistance.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Mystery surrounds death of Class 12 student found burnt behind Delhi school guard room
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old Class 12 student was found in a burnt condition behind a school’s guard room in Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old Class 12 student was found in a burnt condition behind a school’s guard room in Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday.Delhi Police said they received a PCR call about a fire at the school. Personnel from Krishna Nagar police station reached the spot and found the student in a burnt condition.During preliminary proceedings, police recovered certain materials from the scene and the student’s school bag. The crime team was called to inspect the spot and collect evidence.The girl’s elder sister told reporters that she had accompanied her to school to drop her off, along with her niece. She said the girl appeared happy and walked into the school smiling.“She was laughing when she went inside. I don’t know what happened after that,” the sister said.She added that she received a call from the school around 12.40pm informing her that something serious had happened. The sister broke down while recounting the incident.Fire officer Anoop Singh said the cause of the fire had not yet been established and that one fire tender had been sent to the school.“We received a call that a child had set a fire inside a school. Upon arriving at the scene and entering the school, we found a child who had been burned, lying behind a water tank. We don’t know her exact age, but she was in the 12th grade. Only one vehicle from our team arrived. It is not yet clear what was used to start the fire. She was taken away by an ambulance; the hospital will be able to provide details on what happened,” he said.BJP MLA Anil Goyal described the incident as unfortunate and said the police and local administration were investigating the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.“This is a major, unfortunate incident. The reasons behind her suicide are a matter for investigation. Our police, the local administration, and officials from the SDM’s office are all looking into it. The body has now been sent for a post-mortem...” he said.A fire official who reached the spot said they received information around 11.58am that a student had allegedly set herself on fire inside the school. “When we entered the school, we found the student in a burnt condition behind a water tank on the left side. articles.title: A creator in the UAE fitted 150 words onto one sticky note, and her unusual writing feat went viral
articles.summary: A small sticky note has helped Pushpajothi Ravikumar turn a childhood ambition into a Guinness World Records achievement.
articles.body: A small sticky note has helped Pushpajothi Ravikumar turn a childhood ambition into a Guinness World Records achievement. The 29-year-old, who works as a senior cloud engineer in the United Arab Emirates, managed to write 150 different words on a single sticky note, setting a record for the most words written on the small piece of paper. Her attempt, completed in Dubai, attracted widespread attention after she shared a video of the feat. The response reached far beyond her immediate circle, drawing interest from viewers, colleagues and family members.How did the UAE creator fit 150 words on one sticky noteAccording to Guinness World Records, Pushpajothi Ravikumar, known as Jothi, achieved the record by carefully selecting words and making efficient use of the limited writing space. Rather than trying to fill the note with long expressions, she chose simple, short words, most of which contained just three letters.The approach allowed her to include more words without making the writing completely unreadable. Although fitting as many words as possible was central to the challenge, legibility remained an important consideration. Jothi explained to Guinness World Records that she had to establish a limit because the words still needed to be read.The record was not simply a matter of filling every available gap with ink. It required her to balance the number of words against the space available, ensuring that the finished note could still be understood.On 19 August 2026, Guinness World Records identified Jothi as the record holder for writing 150 different words on one sticky note. The achievement took place in Dubai and marked a significant personal milestone for the UAE-based engineer.What inspired Jothi to attempt the unusual writing challengeJothi's interest in record-breaking began long before she decided to attempt the sticky-note challenge. In her interview with Guinness World Records, she explained that she had watched the organisation's records since childhood and dreamed of becoming part of its collection of record holders.Seeing other people achieve unique feats inspired her, although she did not initially know which achievement might eventually become her own. The idea of writing an extraordinary number of words on a tiny piece of paper eventually came to her, prompting her to apply for the record attempt.The official Guinness World Records report also noted that Jothi enjoys experimenting with different handwriting styles. That interest gave her a natural starting point for a challenge that depended on how efficiently she could use a limited area of paper.Despite the unusual nature of the task, she did not need several attempts to secure the title. According to Guinness World Records, she broke the record on her first attempt, making the result particularly rewarding.The sticky-note world record attracted massive online attentionThe achievement gained another dimension when Jothi shared a video of her attempt on Instagram. What began as a personal milestone soon reached a much wider audience, with the video attracting nearly one million views.The attention extended to people who knew her personally, including family members, friends and colleagues, who began asking her about the accomplishment.The simple materials helped make the feat easy to understand. Viewers did not need specialist equipment to appreciate the difficulty of fitting 150 distinct words into such a small space. The contrast between the size of the note and the number of words written on it gave the attempt its appeal.What does the achievement mean for Jothi's future plansFor Jothi, the record has provided both recognition and a boost in confidence. Speaking to Guinness World Records, she described the platform as a way for people to display talents they might not have realised they possessed. She also expressed the belief that everyone has something unique within them.Although the feat might appear modest compared with records involving extraordinary physical or technical challenges, it carried considerable meaning for someone who had wanted to join the record books since childhood.The response to her attempt also encouraged her to consider further challenges. According to the Guinness World Records report, she is keen to break more records in the future. Her next achievement has not been specified in the reports, but the sticky-note record has given her a starting point.Sticky notes are commonly used for reminders and brief messages, but Jothi's attempt pushed the limits of what could be written on one while keeping the words readable. The method depended on choosing short words and making careful use of the available surface without relying on elaborate equipment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2006, a New York couple lost their nine-day-old daughter in an emergency room; 20 years later, their foundation says it has trained 6,500 physicians, and a joint charity gala has raised nearly $2 million
articles.summary: In July 2006, Phyllis and Andrew Rabinowitz took their newborn daughter, Rebecca, to doctors and an emergency department because she was congested,
articles.body: In July 2006, Phyllis and Andrew Rabinowitz took their newborn daughter, Rebecca, to doctors and an emergency department because she was congested, feeding slowly and having difficulty breathing. Her symptoms were repeatedly diagnosed as a common cold, according to the family’s account published by the R Baby Foundation. Rebecca died on July 21, nine days after her birth. The couple later learned that their daughter had contracted an enteroviral infection, which can be life-threatening in newborns. Her death led them to establish the R Baby Foundation, with the aim of improving emergency medical care for babies and children.Twenty years later, the organisation says it has raised $18 million and trained more than 6,500 physicians across over 1,000 hospitals. On October 21, 2026, it marked the anniversary with a joint fundraising gala in New York City alongside the COPE Foundation, which supports families coping with the death of a loved one. According to the official website of R Baby Foundation, the event raised nearly $2 million. The money will support paediatric emergency-care preparedness and grief-support services for bereaved families.How Rebecca’s death led to the foundationRebecca was born four weeks prematurely on July 13, 2006, according to R Baby Foundation’s website. She spent five days in a neonatal intensive care unit before being discharged. The next day, her parents noticed severe congestion, thick mucus, slow feeding and breathing difficulties. They sought medical attention, including at a hospital emergency department, but Rebecca was sent home after her symptoms were assessed as a common cold, the family said.She died on the morning of July 21. The family later learned that the illness was an enteroviral infection. The Rabinowitzes established R Baby Foundation in 2006 to address gaps in the training, equipment and procedures used to treat babies and children in emergency settings. The organisation funds medical education, research, training and equipment, working with children's hospitals to help improve care in community hospitals, where many children receive emergency treatment.What the foundation says it has achieved in 20 yearsR Baby Foundation says it has raised more than $18 million and trained over 6,500 physicians across more than 1,000 hospitals since its establishment. It also says its work reaches more than one million children annually through partnerships with medical institutions, including Yale, Columbia, Johns Hopkins and Mount Sinai. The organisation has established INSPIRE, which it describes as the world's largest paediatric simulation-based research network. Its programmes focus on helping medical professionals recognise and respond to emergencies involving babies and children. The foundation is also pushing for wider policy changes.According to its website, its advocacy has contributed to paediatric emergency-readiness legislation in Texas, Florida and Utah. It is supporting the proposed Babies’ and Children’s Emergency Care Act, known as BECA, which aims to strengthen emergency-care preparedness nationally. R Baby Foundation says about 2,100 children die each year in emergency departments that are not adequately prepared to treat them. It also cites estimates that 83% of US emergency departments lack the equipment, training or protocols needed for paediatric emergencies, despite approximately 30 million paediatric emergency-room visits annually.Why another foundation joined the galaThe event also supported COPE Foundation, short for Connecting Our Paths Eternally, which works with parents, siblings and families grieving the loss of a loved one. COPE was founded by Lillian Julien after her 20-year-old daughter, Michelle, died in a car accident in 1992. In her founder’s statement on COPE’s website, Julien describes how the loss inspired her to create a support network for grieving families.COPE now offers professionally facilitated support groups, workshops, retreats, educational resources and bereavement camps. Its programmes are intended to help parents and children cope with grief alongside people who have experienced similar losses. According to the gala announcement, COPE served more than 1,100 families and individuals in 2025.The two organisations approach loss from different directions. R Baby Foundation works to improve emergency care in the hope of preventing avoidable tragedies, while COPE supports people living with the aftermath of a death.Nearly $2 million raised at New York galaThe October 21 event, called Cirquetacular, brought around 500 supporters, physicians, advocates and families to Capitale in New York City. It marked 20 years of R Baby Foundation’s work and raised nearly $2 million for the two organisations, according to the announcement. The evening included dinner, a live auction, an aerial performance and a fundraising appeal. CC Capital and law firm Skadden were the presenting sponsors, and singer Jac Ross performed at the close of the event.For the Rabinowitzes, the anniversary marked two decades of work that began after Rebecca’s death. The foundation’s stated goal remains to make emergency departments across the United States better prepared to care for children, while its partnership with COPE also directs support towards families who have lost someone they love.You use AI every day.
