articles.title: A dangerous El Niño could turn hunger into famine
articles.summary: The developing El Niño could push millions more people into hunger.
articles.body:
Much of the world’s attention today is fixed on election campaigns, polls, predictions and political battles. Headlines are dominated by who is up, who is down and what comes next.

But while candidates compete for votes, another race is unfolding far from the campaign trail: a race against hunger that millions of families are in danger of losing.

Today, more than 266 million people face acute food insecurity. Yet hunger rarely becomes a headline until it reaches catastrophic levels. By the time images of starving children appear on our screens, families have often been suffering for months, even years.

Famine doesn’t arrive all at once. It arrives slowly, harvest by harvest, meal by meal, until suddenly the world is asking how things got so bad.

The warning signs are already here. Now, a new threat is gathering strength.

Recent forecasts warn that the developing 2026-27 El Niño weather phenomenon could bring drought, flooding, crop losses and rising food insecurity across some of the world’s most vulnerable regions. East and Southern Africa are among the areas of particular concern, where additional climate shocks could drive sharply higher humanitarian needs.

Frontline international humanitarian organizations are reaching a similar conclusion: the developing El Niño could push millions more people into hunger, with particularly severe consequences for women and girls , children and communities already affected by conflict and displacement . Their analyses point to growing food and nutrition risks and worsening food insecurity in places such as Somalia .

Parents are skipping meals so their children can eat. Families are selling livestock and other assets to survive. Children are leaving school, while communities that have already endured conflict, displacement and economic hardship are being pushed closer to the edge.

Now, a new threat is gathering strength.

Recent forecasts warn that the developing 2026-27 El Niño could bring drought, flooding, crop losses and rising food insecurity across some of the world’s most vulnerable regions. East and Southern Africa are among the areas of particular concern, where additional climate shocks could drive sharply higher humanitarian needs.

The danger is not drought alone. It is the collision of multiple crises.

Conflict continues to disrupt food production and trade. Economic pressures are driving up the costs of food, fertilizer and transportation . At the same time, humanitarian resources are shrinking just as needs are increasing. For millions of families already struggling to recover from previous shocks, there is little margin left.

But hunger is one of the few global crises we can often see coming. Early warning systems provide something rare in humanitarian response: a chance to act before lives are lost and communities are pushed into catastrophe.

In fact, some early action is underway. The U.S. government recently announced additional support to help Peru prepare for El Niño-related impacts, underscoring a simple truth: acting on early warnings saves lives and reduces the far greater costs of responding after a crisis takes hold. But more is needed.

Across the globe, American humanitarian organizations are already working alongside local partners to help communities prepare for additional shocks. They are supporting farmers, strengthening local food systems, protecting livelihoods and helping vulnerable families withstand crises. These efforts rarely make headlines, but they can determine whether a shock becomes a hardship or a humanitarian disaster.

As Congress and the administration make decisions about funding and priorities for the year ahead, they face a straightforward choice: act on the warnings we already have or wait until preventable suffering becomes a full-blown humanitarian emergency that is far more costly, both financially and humanly.

Hunger is not inevitable. We know the warning signs. We know what works. The question is whether we choose to act before today’s warning becomes tomorrow’s crisis.

Tom Hart is president and CEO of InterAction, the national alliance of U.S.-based nongovernmental organizations.

articles.title: Iran says won’t allow US warships to get close as Trump ponders new attacks
articles.summary: Iranian officials, media and analysts sense war is closer, but signal there will be no backing down.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Iran’s armed forces say they are prepared to fire on United States warships as President Donald Trump said Washington was still deliberating new attacks or continued pressure on Iran.

Trump told supporters at a rally in Florida on Friday that the US military “may do another Epic Fury”, in reference to the extensive bombing campaign against Iran at the start of the war. He had earlier questioned whether to end the conflict quickly through huge attacks on Iran or let pressure on Tehran from a naval blockade and sanctions persist.

But Ali Abdollahi, chief of general staff of the Iranian armed forces, asserted that the US Navy is incapable of re-entering Iran’s territorial waters or its periphery due to Iran’s ability to target any vessel in the region.

“The US president can only dream of their soldiers and military again entering the Persian Gulf. They will take this wish to the grave for good,” he said in a statement carried by state media on Saturday morning.

Abdollahi also said US rhetoric about the war pointed to a basic contradiction: US claims that Iran’s military capabilities have been mostly destroyed during the war were nullified by its refusal to bring its aircraft carriers and support vessels closer to Iranian territory.

He added that Iranian forces were determined to “drown” the US and Israel in a “quagmire” in retaliation for their surprise attack on Iran on February 28, starting an eight-month war and plunging the whole region into instability.

Vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue to be attacked by Iran. Together with the increased odds of renewed war, this has driven up oil prices and sent Brent crude to its highest price since April, at about $117.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said seven tankers were attacked or hit mines overnight into Thursday. It then claimed on Friday that two supertankers struck mines. The IRGC has said its military doctrine is now more offensive, and Washington has reportedly ordered many diplomatic personnel to leave Saudi Arabia, with others set to depart other countries in the region .

The Iran-allied Houthis in Yemen also continued to exchange attacks with Saudi Arabia, hitting Riyadh again on Saturday, with the international airport in Dammam and the Shaybah oilfield targeted in recent days. Saudi forces have bombed Marib, Taiz and several other Yemeni provinces under Houthi control.

In southern Lebanon, Friday brought further reported Israeli air attacks around Nabatieh and artillery fire near Zawtar ash-Sharqiyah. Iran has linked this front to its war with the US and Israel, in the past demanding that any ceasefire with Washington also cover Lebanon .

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, facing an election on October 27 which comes days before the November 3 mid-term elections in the US, also ordered a lockdown of the occupied West Bank after a Palestinian attack killed two soldiers in Hebron. The Houthis have also launched attacks on Israel linked to events in Gaza and the West Bank, highlighting how wider regional peace now depends on events in multiple theatres, including Lebanon, the occupied West Bank and Gaza.

Netanyahu has reiterated his desire to overthrow the Iranian government, leading several state-linked media and analysts in Iran to claim that Tehran has activated a “dead hand” doctrine. That allegedly enables military attacks against US, Israeli and regional interests to continue from across the country’s 31 provinces if senior Iranian figures are again assassinated as at the start of the war .

The IRGC has threatened seabed internet and communication cables if Iran’s civilian infrastructure is again targeted by the US and Israel. US-based Axios on Saturday cited US intelligence claiming that Iranian authorities had “substantially increased” efforts to strike American officials in the Middle East and beyond.

Mediated negotiations between Iran and the US are no closer to yielding results. But regional and European powers held a coordination meeting in Istanbul on Friday and announced their expectations for the future of the war.

Top diplomats from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt met with the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Italy, with neither the US nor Iran participating.

“We agree that a new attack on Iran would widen the war and spread the conflict across the region,” Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said after the meeting. “Military intervention in Iran is by no means a solution. No one is endorsing it at this point.”

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said his government held Iran and the Houthis responsible for instability in the Middle East.

But the foreign ministers of the four regional countries issued a joint statement that said “Israeli occupation was the main source of instability in the region and beyond.”

In line with resolving the US-Israel war on Iran, the four regional countries supported the Islamabad memorandum of understanding signed in June and a negotiated settlement, while demanding unrestricted passage through the Strait of Hormuz . The group said they opposed attacks on civilians and commercial vessels, and condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and its Red Sea shipping interests.

The Istanbul meeting once again displayed a “gap between diplomatic claims and realities in the field”, Nour News, an outlet affiliated with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, argued in an analysis on Saturday.

It said the US and European powers – not Iran – must make concessions first. The outlet presented reopening the Strait of Hormuz as conditional on the US accepting Tehran’s demands and acknowledging responsibility for attacking Iran and Yemen.

Most Iranian newspapers on Saturday focused on signs of war, including rising oil prices.

The headline from hardline Vatan-e Emrooz reported that the price of a barrel of Brent crude rising above $117 was “evidence of disgrace for Trump”. Reformist Etemad said US and Israeli actions were signalling that the “zero hour” of another intense round of the war was approaching.

Reza Nasri, a Tehran-based foreign policy analyst with links to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that after being subject to decades of attacks, nuclear sabotage, sanctions and violated deals by the US, Iran’s strategy was now “enough is enough.

“Iran has reached its verdict. It will no longer negotiate under bombardment, honour agreements the other side treats as optional, or accept the killing of its children and the penury of its people as routine instruments of policy,” he wrote on X. “It will put an end to this cycle, and it will do so by all necessary means”.

articles.title: Met Police says letter with claims about Meghan's father not shared with other law enforcement
articles.summary: The Met said it passed information to the duchess but did not share it with other law enforcement agencies.
articles.body:
A letter making a "number of claims" relating to the Duchess of Sussex's father was received by the Metropolitan Police in 2019, Scotland Yard has confirmed.

The Met said it passed the information relating to allegations outside the UK to the office of the Duke and Duchess but did not share it with other law enforcement agencies.

It was reported on Friday that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Thomas Markle, 82, had been found in his former home in the Philippines. Markle, who is based in the US, denies possessing any such images.

On Friday, Meghan said she was informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father in 2018. The Met said it was reviewing the matter and deciding whether to refer itself to the police watchdog.

Responding to Saturday's developments dating the letter to 2019, a spokesman for the duchess said "any discrepancy of a few months" was "an understandable consequence of that passage of time".

The claims were first carried by the Sun newspaper, which later said that the letter made direct allegations of child sex abuse against Markle.

In a statement, Scotland Yard said: "Following a thorough review of Met Police systems and records, we have confirmed that in January 2019, we received a letter containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.

"It was sent to the MPS Protection Command to raise concerns in relation to the security of the Duchess of Sussex.

"The letter was reviewed and a decision was made that it should be passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness. The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies.

"The MPS is reviewing the handling of this matter in 2019 and considering whether a referral to the IOPC is necessary to review our approach."

Markle moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes.

He is reportedly now living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having a leg amputated in 2025.

Meghan's half-brother Thomas Markle Jnr claimed he found a stash of images belonging to his father at his former Philippines home, the Sun reported.

He is said to have told police he discovered child abuse videos and pictures among the items. He is understood to have contacted the FBI in July.

In a statement released by Meghan on Friday she said that when she received the information of the claims against her father she was "given assurance that these were being investigated".

Meghan said she hoped it could be understood why she had kept her distance from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Authorities in the Philippines have confirmed they are investigating the allegations about Meghan's father.

The BBC was told on Friday the matter was being investigated by an anti-human trafficking and child sexual exploitation task force.

Philippines Interior Minister Jonvic Remulla separately said national police had secured his computer and would carry out a digital forensic examination.

Meghan is the only daughter of Markle and her mother Doria Ragland.

He pulled out of attending Meghan and Harry's wedding in 2018 - citing ill health - and they became estranged.

The duke and duchess moved to the US in 2020 after stepping down as working royals.

They returned to the UK with their children this year after six years away.

articles.title: Child poverty in Wales - Daughter slept on bed propped up by books
articles.summary: Sarah Ruscoe, a single mum out of work due to health issues, worried her daughter’s bed would collapse at night.
articles.body:
"I was sleeping on the sofa, she had a bed that was propped up on books. One of the legs had fallen off completely."

Sarah Ruscoe, a single mum out of work because of a health condition, said she had worried her daughter's bed would collapse in the night after finding herself in a "dire" financial situation.

A food bank user, Ruscoe said "every year seems to be getting worse" as she struggled to make her benefits cover essentials.

A charity eventually paid for a new bed for daughter Sabrina, 11.

But MPs heard this week that the general picture of one in three children living in relative poverty in Wales had not changed in 20 years, with a think tank saying the problem was becoming entrenched.

'There's so much I want to give my daughter - poverty means I can't'

£10-a-week child poverty payment plans faces obstacles, says expert

On Wednesday MPs at the UK Parliament's Welsh Affairs Committee opened an inquiry on ending child poverty in Wales.

The country has the highest child poverty rate of any UK nation, with 32% of children living in relative poverty after housing costs, according to the latest official statistics.

A child is considered to be in relative poverty if the income of the household they live in is below 60% of the UK median.

Evidence was given by charities including Action for Children, who paid for Sabrina's new bed and provides financial support to thousands of low income families in Wales each year.

Ruscoe, from Barry, told BBC Wales that three years ago she struggled to afford to replace her daughter's "ropey" bed which had been "second or third hand".

"It was getting a bit distressing," she said, and both mother and daughter had worried it might collapse in the night when Sabrina moved.

"I was having difficulty finding somewhere where I could afford one, and also not having the greatest credit rating in the world meant that you had to pay like two or three times what you would have done if you'd just gone into a shop and bought it outright."

The cabin bunk and a mattress purchased by Action for Children made a "massive difference", she said.

"It meant she had somewhere safe. It's a little nest now. We decorated it," Ruscoe said.

"Nobody else has slept in it. It's something that's new for her.

"Up until that point it was worry and trying to work out, maybe if I didn't pay this bill maybe I could save some money here, what could I go without, trying to work out which company had the smallest APR on an item that I could afford.

"There's not that much out there, especially when they hear you're on benefits."

One year the charity also helped the family with a gift card for local supermarkets before Christmas.

Ruscoe, who used to work in a job centre, said her chronic pain condition fibromyalgia had left her feeling fatigued and in pain and, when it had flared up, unable to move.

"I don't work due to my disabilities so it's a case of benefits, and that's how we survive, and this year seems to be worse than last year. Every year seems to be getting worse.

"Last year I managed to put money away over the course of the year for Christmas and this year I haven't been able to at all. Everything has gone up.

"There's only so much penny pinching you can do on everything and then realise that every penny you've pinched is still not covering all your bills and your outgoings."

Ruscoe warned that anyone could find themselves in a crisis situation because of ill-health or an unexpected life event.

Laurie Ryall, Wales director at Action for Children, gave evidence to MPs on the first day of their inquiry in Westminster, and said the absence of a single point of access for support had often left families experiencing child poverty feeling overwhelmed.

"They don't always know what they're entitled to or where to go, it's confusing, it's a minefield," Ryall said.

Mabli Jones from the Bevan Foundation think tank told MPs that although child poverty had remained at the same level for two decades "what's been happening under the surface is that poverty has got deeper".

"Almost half - 47% - of people in Wales who live in poverty live in what's classed as very deep poverty - that's an income that is at or below 40% of the median," she said.

"Families who are experiencing that kind of poverty are likely to be going without many of the basics."

A UK government spokesperson said: "We're determined to turn the tide on poverty, and our landmark child poverty strategy will lift 550,000 children out of poverty in the final year of this parliament - the largest reduction in child poverty since records began."

They said abolishing the two-child limit would benefit an estimated 69,000 children in Wales, and a temporary cut to electricity bills and raising the National Living Wage had contributed to a fall in food bank usage.

A Welsh government spokesperson said it had "inherited a damning legacy of stubbornly high levels of child poverty".

It said it was helping families through the first phase of its offer of 12.5 hours of free childcare to all two-year-olds and extending free school meals.

They also said the government was seeking assurance from the UK government that a proposed pilot scheme for £10 a week to each child to support low-income families would not affect families' benefit payments.

"We continue to call on the UK government to use all the levers at its disposal, including those on welfare, to make a lasting difference to families in Wales," they said.

articles.title: Paris shuts Louvre and other museums as police deploy in big numbers for new protests across France
articles.summary: PARIS — Thousands of students and workers marched in Paris and other French cities Saturday over school funding and soaring living costs.
articles.body: PARIS — Thousands of students and workers marched in Paris and other French cities Saturday over school funding and soaring living costs. Police used tear gas in Lyon, where the rally had been banned, on Saturday morning. In Clermont-Ferrand, officers used tear gas and stun grenades to push back demonstrators trying to reach the city center, French media reported. Authorities had confined the Paris march to the city’s southeastern edge, away from the center. Several thousand people marched from Porte d’Italie early in the afternoon, a smaller crowd than a week earlier. Trade unions led the procession, followed by protesters in raincoats carrying flags and handmade placards. Authorities sought to prevent another weekend of looting, burned cars and attacks on public buildings. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said up to 70,000 officers would be deployed nationwide, backed by helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons. Thousands also marched Saturday in Orléans, south of Paris, in a separate peaceful protest against the far right as Marine Le Pen’s National Rally held a two-day congress in the city. A small protest became a national movement What began last month as a protest over staff shortages at one high school southeast of Paris has grown into a national movement. Students demanding better schools and workers seeking higher wages and pensions have brought anger over living standards into the final months of President Emmanuel Macron’s presidency. Energy prices in France were 21.3% higher in September than a year earlier, helping drive overall inflation to 3.1%, according to the national statistics agency, INSEE. Macron met high school representatives Friday. They said he had promised to overhaul university admissions, but called for protests to continue until concrete measures are announced. More than half a million people took to the streets last Saturday. Some 3,000 shops across France were damaged or looted over the weekend. Shops board up and museums close Gendarmes stood guard beneath the Arc de Triomphe as shopkeepers boarded up storefronts across Paris. Near the Saint-Lazare train station Saturday, Akram Ahmed, a 34-year-old contractor, was boarding up an optician’s shop. “I got the call last night,” he said. “The owner seemed desperate. He said I was saving his life.” Major museums, including the Louvre, Orsay Museum, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais — where a major Cézanne exhibit is on display — were shuttered Saturday. Art Basel, one of the world’s most prestigious contemporary art fairs, opened to the public Friday, but only for the day, with the threat of unrest prompting organizers to cancel the weekend program. Some protests have been banned Police changed the Paris route Friday, replacing the planned Bastille-to-Nation march with a route between Porte d’Italie and Porte de Vincennes. At Bastille, the original starting point, police used a megaphone to tell people to leave or face a 135-euro ($150) fine. Soumaya Abed, a 58-year-old nurse wearing a red CGT union vest, said she had been joining protests for more than 30 years but had never seen a march start at Porte d’Italie. “They are using what happened last week as an excuse to quiet protesters,” she said. “But it won’t stop the movement. It won’t stop students from demanding better conditions in schools.” Protest marches are scheduled in Paris and Marseille, but some other rallies, including in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, have been banned by local authorities. Trade unions have criticized the bans, calling them violations of freedom of expression, which is protected by the constitution. Macron, a centrist, has entered the crisis in the final stretches of his term with his popularity at its lowest since he took office in 2017. He has said that the measures are needed to protect city centers, businesses and public buildings. Nuñez acknowledged Monday that police had lost control in some cities during last weekend’s unrest. He offered to resign, but Macron refused the offer. Students and workers are angry Student groups want 250,000 more places in higher education and an end to selection through Parcoursup, the national admissions system. Their joint 10-point plan also calls for more teachers and repairs to schools and universities. Public middle and high schools lost 15.4 million teaching hours in the 2024-25 school year because absent teachers were not replaced, according to Education Ministry figures. That amounted to 7.5% of scheduled teaching time. They are also seeking help with everyday costs: an extra 200 euros a month in student grants and a rent freeze in public student housing. “The money is now concentrated in the hands of very few people,” said Victoria Ambrosini, an art critic and art teacher at Saint-Denis University.

articles.title: Thousands without power as South West stormy weather continues
articles.summary: A heavy rain warning is in place until 23:00, as a cafe welcomes people with no power.
articles.body:
Thousands of homes are without power, and disruption is continuing across Devon and Cornwall after more stormy weather.

On Friday, Storm Austen battered the south-west of England before moving to other parts of the UK.

On Saturday, the Met Office issued a yellow weather warning for heavy rain from 11:00 BST until 23:00 for the South West, in association with Storm Boelo.

In Devon and Cornwall, flights and trains have been cancelled. The National Grid said more than 3,200 properties were without power in Cornwall, and more than 760 in Devon.

Skybus said flights remained on hold due to adverse weather conditions, and due to a tree blocking the railway between Exeter St Davids and Okehampton the line was closed.

Near Truro, the Arborist cafe, has been welcoming people who do not have power in their homes.

Louise Martin, co-owner, said: "We do this for the storms now, we did it in Storm Goretti, we've got a free tea and coffee station with water and biscuits.

"People can come down and there's no pressure to buy anything here.

She said: "You can help yourself to tea and coffee, bring a book, we've got games here... and you can charge your phones and devices, and if you want, bring flasks and things to fill up with hot water."

"It's a bit miserable being at home and being cold," she added.

Julie and Andrew Le Masurier said they had been without power since early Friday morning and they were not expecting it to be back on until Sunday.

Julia said they had their own water supply so were unable to pump the water.

"It was a brilliant surprise to walk in here and find out that they've just got open house and free tea and coffee and stay as long as you like," she said.

"It's lovely, lovely thing to do for the community."

Linda Jane Ludlow, BBC Weather Presenter, said: "As the second storm in two days sweeps across the country, Storm Boelo is bringing some persistent rain, at times heavy, for the rest of the afternoon and then this evening we will see a band or particularly heavy and squally showers from early evening in the south west and west, clearing the region by midnight.

"The likelihood of surface water flooding, alongside gusty southwest veering northwest strong winds with gusts up to 50 mph (80 km/h) in the far southwest and 45-50mph (72 km/h - 80 km/h) in the west, will make conditions challenging for driving.

"Overnight, a weak ridge of high pressure moves in with drier conditions. Tomorrow will be drier and brighter with sunny spells but still with some gusty strong winds, which will decrease in strength throughout the afternoon."

articles.title: A New York husband used a loan secured against his own home to help buy a marital property; after the couple divorced, an October 22 court ruled the debt must be paid from their joint home's sale proceeds
articles.summary: A New York appeals court has ruled that a husband who borrowed money against a home he owned before marriage is entitled to have that debt paid in full
articles.body: A New York appeals court has ruled that a husband who borrowed money against a home he owned before marriage is entitled to have that debt paid in full from the proceeds of selling the couple's jointly owned marital home. The ruling was issued on 22 October 2026 by the New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department, in the divorce case Menkes v Menkes. The decision explains how New York's divorce laws treat debts taken on by one spouse to buy a shared family home. It clarifies how these financial obligations must be handled when a couple divorces and their property is divided. According to court filings published by the Appellate Division, First Department, the husband owned a residential property in his name alone before the marriage. During the marriage, the couple decided to buy a new home together as jointly owned marital property. To pay for the purchase, the husband took out a home equity loan using his separately owned property as security. He directed the full loan amount toward buying the new family home.Court confirms equitable distribution principleAfter the marriage broke down and divorce proceedings began, the couple disagreed over how the remaining home equity loan debt should be handled when their marital assets were divided. The First Department judges ruled that because the borrowed money was used only to buy the jointly owned family home, the debt counted as a shared marital liability. As a result, the court ordered that when the marital home is sold, the proceeds must first be used to repay the home equity loan secured against the husband's separate property. Any money left over can then be divided between the former spouses. The court explained that refusing to repay the husband from the sale proceeds would unfairly penalize him for using his own property to help buy a shared family asset. Under New York's rules for dividing property in a divorce, courts must fairly divide both marital assets and marital debts. They consider the direct financial contributions each spouse made during the marriage.Rights over separate assets reaffirmedThe Appellate Division also clarified that taking out a loan against property owned separately by one spouse does not automatically turn that property into a marital asset. This applies as long as the borrowed money can be clearly traced to the purchase of the jointly owned home. Family law attorneys note that the ruling supports an important principle in complex, high-value divorces across New York. When one spouse uses separate property or personal credit to help create a shared marital asset, the debt is linked to the asset it helped purchase rather than remaining solely the responsibility of the person who borrowed the money. The Appellate Division's decision formally changes the lower court's divorce judgment. articles.title: North Korea’s Kim crosses new bridge into China as trade ties warm
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, Xinhua reported, crossing a newly opened bridge in a symbolic move seen as highlighting Beijing and Pyongyang’s push to expand trade ties.
articles.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, Xinhua reported, crossing a newly opened bridge in a symbolic move seen as highlighting Beijing and Pyongyang’s push to expand trade ties. Kim was accompanied during his visit by China’s fourth-highest-ranked official Wang Huning, who conveyed greetings from President Xi Jinping, the official Xinhua news agency said. Kim arrived in Dandong via the New Yalu River Bridge connecting North Korea and China, a South Korean government official said on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly. The new bridge is expected to help move heavy equipment, raw materials and energy products that North Korea needs for development. Its official opening this month is the latest sign of warming ties between Beijing and Pyongyang, after two summits between their leaders in the past 13 months. China, which fought alongside North Korea in the 1950-1953 Korean War, remains Pyongyang’s main economic and diplomatic backer and accounts for most of its official trade. Chinese TV shows Kim walking on bridge But North Korea’s deepening military ties with Russia since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine have led analysts to question whether Pyongyang is becoming less reliant on Beijing. Kim’s trip nevertheless points to a renewed push by China and North Korea to bolster their economic relationship. South Korea’s Yonhap news agency had earlier reported that Kim was expected to return to North Korea after Saturday’s visit. Footage from Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed Kim walking on the bridge, lined by people waving flags, towards North Korea. Xinhua said Wang accompanied Kim to a Korean War memorial in Dandong, where the North Korean leader paid tribute to Chinese People’s Volunteer Army soldiers who fought alongside North Korea during the three-year conflict. Kim also toured a Dandong automobile factory, it said. New Yalu River Bridge boosts bilateral ties China and North Korea opened the 3 km (2 mile) New Yalu River Bridge, their most significant land border crossing, this month after a long delay, aiming to rejuvenate trade and commerce after years of strained ties and ‌pandemic-related disruptions. “Kim has given his imprimatur to bilateral trade by crossing the New Yalu River Bridge to enter China,” said Christopher Green, a Korea specialist at Leiden University in the Netherlands, saying the delayed opening had shown how dysfunctional the relationship had become. During a meeting on Saturday, Wang told Kim that China was ready to use the bridge’s opening to expand personnel exchanges and economic and trade cooperation, Xinhua said. A visit by Kim now is consistent with the current phase of closer economic ties and more frequent high-level exchanges between China and North Korea, said Lu Chao, an expert in China-North Korea relations at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, a Chinese government think-tank in Shenyang. “The opening of the bridge has resolved a major bottleneck in China-North Korea trade logistics,” Lu said. “With the logistics constraint eased, bilateral trade is likely to increase further.” Trump waits for Kim to engage Kim’s last known visit to China was in September 2025, to attend the 80th Victory Day celebrations in Beijing, when he held a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Xi made a state visit to North Korea in June. US President Donald Trump has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but US and South Korean officials see fading chances of him meeting Kim this year, Reuters reported on Friday. China hosts a summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum next month in Shenzhen, which Trump is expected to attend.

articles.title: North Bengaluru areas battle power cuts for 3 months as Metro work damages Bescom cable
articles.summary: North Bengaluru faces 3 months of power cuts after Metro construction damaged a Bescom underground cable; repair delayed amid Bescom-BMRCL cost dispute.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A damaged underground power cable that has remained unrepaired for nearly three months has emerged as a major cause of recurring power cuts and poor power supply quality in parts of north Bengaluru.The damage, caused during BMRCL’s Metro pillar construction work near Pruthvi Theatre on Nagawara Ring Road, has raised questions about the agency’s failure to restore critical power infrastructure despite repeated complaints and requests from Bescom engineers.According to a complaint filed by Bescom engineers with Sampigehalli police stationon June 6, a copy of which was accessed by TOI, a 400 sq mm underground cable belonging to Bescom’s feeder F11 LRB was severely damaged on June 4.“The feeder supplies electricity to Nagawara Residency and surrounding areas. Despite repeated communications seeking restoration, the damaged cable remains unrepaired, forcing Bescom to rely on an alternative feeder that struggles to cope with the increasing load from nearby areas,” a Bescom engineer said.Flagging the operational constraints caused by the damage, Bescom engineers said the fallout extends across a 2-3 km radius, affecting Nagawara Ring Road, parts of Thanisandra Main Road, Manyata Tech Park, Manyata Residency, parts of Rachenahalli and Veeranna Palya.“We have been facing significant operational difficulties in maintaining an uninterrupted power supply to consumers in the affected areas, resulting in inconvenience to the public and potential risks to the power distribution system,” the engineers stated in their complaint.In the meantime, Bescom engineers’ efforts to manage the situation through an alternative feeder have also failed, with the transmission network witnessing an overload due to a surge in power demand.Although the complaint named the BMRCL engineers and contractors allegedly responsible for the damage and disruption to power supply, police did not register an FIR, according to Bescom officials.Bescom estimated the value of the damaged cable and associated assets at Rs 10 lakh, with revenue losses of about Rs 20 lakh. “Despite repeated requests and communications to the BMRCL authorities, no action has been taken so far,” the engineers said in their complaint.Repair held hostage by cost disputeWith the issue dragging on for nearly three months, the standoff between the two govt agencies has left the public caught in the crossfire, forced to endure recurring power cuts. BMRCL engineers said the corporation had initially asked Bescom to repair the cable, with the Metro agency offering to reimburse the expenditure later. Bescom, however, insisted that the contractor responsible for the damage undertake the repair and replacement of the entire cable.“The Bescom engineers refused to carry out the repairs and insisted that our contractor replace the entire damaged cable. articles.title: Deadly Siwan blast puts state’s illegal cracker network under fresh scrutiny
articles.summary: Siwan firecracker blast kills 5 in Bihar, reviving scrutiny of hidden illegal cracker-making units; similar incidents statewide and NCRB data highlight risks.
articles.body: Patna: The deadly firecracker explosion in Siwan has once again put Bihar’s hidden and potentially lethal cracker-making network under the scanner. Five people were killed and three others injured after firecrackers stored in a house at Alampur village under Jamo Bazar police station caught fire on Friday, triggering explosions that continued for hours.The Siwan blast is particularly alarming as the district witnessed a similar incident just nine months earlier. On Jan 22, 2026, a blast occurred inside a house in Bargam village under Hussainganj police station where firecrackers were allegedly being manufactured illegally. A 50-year-old man, Murtazza Ansari, was killed and three members of his family were injured.The problem is not confined to Siwan. On Sept 25, an explosion in Bhargama police station area of Araria district was found by police to have occurred during illegal firecracker manufacturing. Gunpowder reportedly exploded during the process, killing three people, including two women and a one-month-old child.The trail goes back further. In Oct 2025, a firecracker explosion in Ulhanpur village under Marhaura police station in Saran killed one person. In May 2024, a high-intensity blast at Motirajpur under Garkha police station in Saran killed Mohammad Imamuddin, an imam, and injured a 15-year-old boy. Police found indications of gunpowder or explosive material at the site.Official accident data also reflects the danger. The National Crime Records Bureau’s Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India (ADSI) 2023 report recorded eight cases in Bihar under “Fire in Factory Manufacturing Combustible Materials Including Cracker/Match Box Factories”. The incidents left eight people dead and two injured. Bihar recorded the second-highest number of such cases after Tamil Nadu, while India recorded 52 cases.In 2022, Bihar recorded nine cases under the same category, resulting in one death and eight injuries. The NCRB figures, however, do not necessarily capture the total number of illegal firecracker units in the state.Bihar ADG (headquarters) Sunil Kumar said regular drives and inspections are conducted by police and local administration, particularly ahead of Diwali and New Year. “Only licensed firecracker units operating outside populated areas and complying with licence conditions are permitted. However, some people manufacture firecrackers secretly and illegally in their homes. Following the Siwan incident, SPs have been directed to conduct regular drives and inspections, especially in view of Diwali,” he told this newspaper on Saturday.In Oct 2025, Patna Police raided an alleged illegal firecracker factory in Taranagar village in Bihta and seized around 392kg of explosive material. Four people were arrested. Police recovered potassium, sulphur, charcoal powder, cracker shells and other materials used to manufacture firecrackers. articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders take legal action against My Chemical Romance over onstage costumes
articles.summary: The parent company of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders is taking legal action against My Chemical Romance after the band performed alongside dancers in costumes resembling the iconic cheerleading team’s uniforms this week.
articles.body: The parent company of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders is taking legal action against My Chemical Romance after the band performed alongside dancers in costumes resembling the iconic cheerleading team’s uniforms this week. Pro Silver Star, which owns the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brand, filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction Friday in district court in Dallas County, Texas, seeking to bar the alternative rock band from using the costumes onstage. My Chemical Romance, best known for its 2000s hits “Teenagers” and “Welcome to the Black Parade,” performed Wednesday at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles with dancers wearing outfits that appeared nearly identical to the squad’s iconic white and blue uniforms, according to the court filing. The dancers carried what appeared to be rifles and engaged in a staged firefight, “only to be depicted being shot,” the filing states. “Audience members and online commentators understandably believed that the performers were the real Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and said so in social media posts that continue to circulate,” Pro Silver Star wrote. The company said it was “not litigious” and “takes no issue with MCR’s music, its artistic ambitions, or any message Defendants seek to convey.” “Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it,” the filing states. “The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited.” Representatives for the band and Pro Silver Star did not immediately respond to requests for comment. My Chemical Romance is on tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of its third studio album, “The Black Parade.” The band is scheduled to perform at the Hollywood Bowl again on Saturday evening and twice over Halloween weekend.
